issue_title: Keep inbound webhook deliveries so support can replay them
issue_body:
When a partner's webhook handler fails, the delivery is lost and support has nothing to replay.

Store every inbound delivery to `POST /hooks/{partner}` with its headers and payload before it is handled. Add `GET /hooks/deliveries/{id}`, returning the stored delivery as JSON with `partner`, `received_at`, `headers` and `payload` so support can inspect it, and `POST /hooks/deliveries/{id}/replay`, which runs the stored delivery through the partner's handler again. An unknown delivery id returns `404` on both routes.

plan.summary: Persist inbound webhook deliveries in hook_deliveries and add inspect and replay routes.

approach.description: Add migration 0041 creating hook_deliveries (id, partner, received_at, headers jsonb, payload jsonb), with a down migration.
In the POST /hooks/{partner} handler, insert the delivery via InsertDelivery before dispatching it to the partner's handler.
Add GET /hooks/deliveries/{id}, returning partner, received_at, headers and payload from the row, or 404.
Add POST /hooks/deliveries/{id}/replay, loading the row and dispatching its headers and payload to the partner's handler, or 404.

verification.test_strategy: Handler tests: a delivery is stored even when its handler fails, the GET returns the stored fields, replay dispatches to a fake handler, and unknown ids return 404 on both routes.
verification.rollback_plan: Revert the PR and run the 0041 down migration; stored deliveries are dropped.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Each POST /hooks/{partner} inserts one hook_deliveries row with the partner, received_at, headers and payload, even when the partner's handler fails.
GET /hooks/deliveries/{id} returns JSON with partner, received_at, headers and payload for a stored delivery.
GET /hooks/deliveries/{id} returns the payload byte-for-byte as received, original whitespace and key order included.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: A replay should send the partner's exact payload, so the stored copy must match what arrived.

acceptance_criteria.statement: POST /hooks/deliveries/{id}/replay dispatches the stored delivery to the partner's handler once.
GET /hooks/deliveries/{id} and POST /hooks/deliveries/{id}/replay for an unknown id return HTTP 404.

risks_and_assumptions: Every partner posts a JSON body.

catching_examples.note: ac-delivery-payload-verbatim cannot pass under the plan's own storage: jsonb normalizes whitespace and key order, so GET can never return the payload byte-for-byte.
ac-delivery-payload-verbatim is not warranted: the issue never asks for a byte-exact payload, only one support can inspect and replay, and the plan cites no place that requires it.
The criterion requiring the payload as received, original whitespace and key order included, is unsatisfiable: approach step 1 stores the payload in a jsonb column.

ac-delivery-payload-verbatim is an inferred, blocking criterion the plan's own design cannot meet: approach step 1 declares payload jsonb, and jsonb does not preserve whitespace, key order or duplicate keys. Either store the raw body in a text or bytea column or drop the criterion; the issue asks only that support can inspect and replay a delivery.

non_catching_examples.note: ac-delivery-payload-verbatim needs a test that posts a payload and compares the GET response with it.
Stored headers may include a partner's Authorization header; redact it before the insert.
ac-delivery-payload-verbatim is ambiguous for a form-encoded delivery; a mismatch with the JSON response shape is unsupported.
Migration 0041 creates hook_deliveries with payload jsonb; add an index on received_at for support's date-range lookups.
ac-delivery-replay: replay dispatches the stored delivery once; also test a replay whose handler fails again.
GET /hooks/deliveries/{id} exposes partner payloads; the plan does not say which callers may read deliveries.
